summary: A picnic forest in the village country south of Ahwa, shade, birdsong and spread-a-mat ground on the Wasurna side of the district.
description:
Maharaychond is the south-western pocket's picnic forest: a stand of shade trees in the village country beyond Temburgartha, where local families spread mats under the canopy and make an unhurried afternoon of it. There is no gate, no fee and no development, the forest itself is the amenity, and the etiquette is the village's: leave nothing, light nothing.

It slots into the pocket's easy circuit, the Wasurna valley vista is three kilometres away, the Temburgartha dam's sunset ridge six, and works best exactly as locals use it: the shaded lunch stop between the pocket's viewpoints and falls.
highlights: Canopy shade and picnic ground in open village country
Three kilometres from the Wasurna valley vista
The natural lunch stop of the south-western circuit

modes.road: The Wasurna-side village roads south from Ahwa
modes.rail: Waghai (heritage narrow gauge); Bilimora Jn for broad gauge

access.last_mile: Level walk from the roadside into the trees

visit.notes: Open forest. Carry everything in and everything out; no fires.

seasonality.notes: Green and cool through monsoon and winter; leafless and hot by late spring.

experience.photography_notes: Canopy light-shafts on clear mornings; birdlife is the quiet draw.

amenities.food: None. Carry the picnic from Ahwa

warnings: No fires: this is standing forest
Carry out all waste; there is no collection of any kind

tips: Make it the lunch stop between the Wasurna vista and the dam's sunset ridge
Weekdays have the shade to yourself; local families claim Sundays
